rated_messages.input_message: Urges are like annoying ads. You might see them but you don't have to buy what they're selling.
You were often stressed in this location and this might trigger urges. What can you do to reduce your stress here? If you can avoid this place until things settle down, then do.
Are you willing to let this urge pass for the sake of living a good long time with the people who matter most to you? When you have an urge, think about the people most important to you.
Ways of dealing with urges: play a game or an online quiz.
If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, keep a pen and paper nearby to occupy your hands with doodling rather than smoking.
If you're stuck at home and physical activity doesn't interest you, try gaming, needlework, drawing, or journaling.
Imagine your 'you' from next year has come to visit, and guess what? You quit! How good is that?
Pause. Notice what triggered you to smoke in the past. Now take one deep breath and remind yourself that you do not need to smoke.

Imagine walking into a social situation in three months' time as a non-smoker. Now hold that picture and imagine you're that person now. Seeing yourself as a non-smoker now can make it much easier to resist!
Stop! Breathe. What is going on around you? Inside you? Allow everything to be just as it is. Breathe again.
